note: R29 adoption inventory: every package whose PRODUCTION source (src/, excluding tests and in-source test blocks) forks fibers, holds Queue/Deferred/Ref/Semaphore state, or acquires scoped resources. Each entry names the primitives the package uses and the check that fits it. The evaluator guard scripts/guards/check-conformance-inventory.ts derives the package set from source and fails when a matching package is missing here, when an entry under-declares its primitives, or when an entry has no adopted check: a *.conformance.test.ts anywhere in the package, a smoke-journey journey file, or a harness self-suite.

checks.linearizable: concurrent operations match some sequential order of a pure model (R6)
checks.sequential: an operation sequence stays in step with a model (R7)
checks.released: interruption at every step leaves nothing held (R8)
checks.smoke-journey: resource release checked against the real system in an end-to-end journey outside the in-process test lane (R26)

harnessRule: A package that IS conformance or test infrastructure cannot adopt a check the way a consumer can; silently excluding it would hide the harness's own untested state. Its entry therefore still names the check its own primitives implement and lists harness.selfSuites — the package's own suites that exercise it — with a why reason. The guard verifies those suites exist instead of a *.conformance.test.ts.

entries.note: Workspace example, not a published package; its in-memory CustomerGate (one Semaphore per customer, created on first use under a Ref-guarded map) is judged linearizable against a pure model of one customer's orders served one at a time.

harness.why: conformance-spec IS the linearizable/sequential/released checks; its own suites exercise those checks against planted-bug fixtures under U6/U7/U8.
differential-spec IS the differential harness; under R13 it runs both sides in the kernel under one generated schedule, so its own suites exercise it through Parity/Metamorphic cases.
